The chapter will help with reading Kullilli words. It’s got a lot of information that will help you 
read the rest of this book. That’s why we put it first. But if you want to start with greetings or

The letters used to spell Kullilli sounds are the same as in English, but some letters (and 
combinations of letters) are pronounced differently from how they are said in English. In 
addition, Kullilli has some sounds that don’t exist in English, so it may take you some 
practice before you feel confident pronouncing them. This section will help you learn the 
letters of the Kullilli alphabet, as well as provide example words in Kullilli and useful tricks for 
remembering the pronunciation of the letters. 
 
Vowels 
We will begin with the vowel sounds of Kullilli. Unlike English, Kullilli only has three vowel 
sounds: a, i, and u. In the chart below, you will find more details on these vowel sounds.

Dental consonants 
Kullilli has four dental consonants: dh, th, nh, and lh. Just like ng, even though these are 
written as two letters, they each make only one sound (similar to how ch makes a single 
sound in English, for example). They are called dental consonants because they are 
pronounced by placing the tip of the tongue between the front teeth. Notice that each of 
them has an h, so you can think of the h as an instruction to put your tongue tip between 
your teeth when you say them. 
 
When pronouncing each of them, your mouth should be making similar sounds as to when 
you pronounce d, t, n, or l in English, with the only difference being that the tip of your 
tongue should not be against the roof of your mouth, but between your teeth. Be careful to 
remember that th in Kullilli is not pronounced the same as in English. Unlike in English, when 
saying th in Kullilli, the airflow in your mouth should stop completely before you “release” the 
sound.

hear the difference between them and d, t, n, and l is just as important and may be more 
difficult. Just like with pronunciation, practice makes perfect with learning to recognize these 
sounds when you hear them. You can find spoken examples of words with these sounds in 
the Kullilli dictionary app.2

Retroflex consonants 
Kullilli also has a set of four retroflex consonants: rd, rt, rn, and rl. They are called retroflex 
consonants because they are pronounced by curling (or “flexing”) the tip of the tongue

your tongue is in this position, you can pronounce rd, rt, rn, or rl just as you would d, t, n, or l.
